questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Deep fascia and Triangles of the neck
questions.question: A surgeon performing a radical neck dissection wants to start at the anterior triangle. Which of the following areas will she not dissect?
questions.explanation: The subclavian triangle is a posterior triangle of the neck, not an anterior triangle. The anterior triangles of the neck are the submental, digastric (submandibular), muscular and carotid triangles. The posterior triangles of the neck are the occipital and subclavian triangles.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The subclavian triangle is a posterior triangle of the neck, not an anterior triangle. The anterior triangles of the neck are the submental, digastric (submandibular), muscular and carotid triangles. The posterior triangles of the neck are the occipital and subclavian triangles.

questions.question: Which of the following structures does not form either the roof or a content of the posterior triangle?
questions.explanation: The suprascapular nerve is a content of the lower part of the posterior triangle of the neck; it does not contribute to its roof. Lesser occipital, supraclavicular and great auricular nerves form part of the cutaneous nerve contents of the posterior triangle.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Deep fascia and Triangles of the neck
questions.question: Which of the following is true about deep cervical fascia?

options.text: Investing layer covers parotid gland and submandibular gland
Pretracheal layer covers both thyroid and parotid gland
Axillary sheath is formed by the pretracheal fascia
Investing layer forms the floor of posterior triangle

questions.correctAnswerText: Investing layer covers parotid gland and submandibular gland
questions.explanation: The investing layer of deep cervical fascia covers the parotid and submandibular glands. The pretracheal fascia encloses the thyroid gland and forms the false capsule; the parotid gland is covered by the superficial lamina of the investing layer. The axillary sheath is formed by the prevertebral fascia, and the investing layer forms the roof rather than the floor of the posterior triangle.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The investing layer of deep cervical fascia covers the parotid and submandibular glands. The pretracheal fascia encloses the thyroid gland and forms the false capsule; the parotid gland is covered by the superficial lamina of the investing layer. The axillary sheath is formed by the prevertebral fascia, and the investing layer forms the roof rather than the floor of the posterior triangle.

questions.question: A 54-year-old woman with papillary thyroid carcinoma developed a palpable lymph node in the suprasternal space of Burns. Which of the following structures is not closely related to these metastatic lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: The external jugular vein is not a content of the suprasternal space of Burns. This space is present in the suprasternal region along with the suprasternal/aponeurotic interval.

questions.question: A 21-year-old student presents with a single episode of loss of consciousness. He was about to give a speech at his graduation ceremony when he suddenly turned pale and collapsed to the ground. Which of the following areas contain the nerve responsible for it?
questions.explanation: The scenario describes a vasovagal syncope. The vagus nerve is a content of the carotid triangle, corresponding to the area marked 4 in the question image.

questions.question: Which of the following branches of the external carotid artery is not given off in the carotid triangle?
questions.explanation: The posterior auricular artery is not given off within the carotid triangle; it arises above the triangle. The remaining listed vessels are branches of the external carotid artery associated with the carotid triangle.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The posterior auricular artery is not given off within the carotid triangle; it arises above the triangle. The remaining listed vessels are branches of the external carotid artery associated with the carotid triangle.

questions.question: You are auscultating for bruit in a patient suspected to have an internal carotid artery stenosis. Which of the following muscles does not form the floor of the triangle you are auscultating?
questions.explanation: Carotid bruit is auscultated over the carotid triangle. Mylohyoid does not form the floor of the carotid triangle.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Carotid bruit is auscultated over the carotid triangle. Mylohyoid does not form the floor of the carotid triangle.

questions.question: Which of the following muscles is not supplied by the structure marked in the image?
questions.explanation: The marked structure is ansa cervicalis. Thyrohyoid is supplied by C1 fibres travelling with the hypoglossal nerve, not by ansa cervicalis. Ansa cervicalis supplies the other listed infrahyoid muscles.

questions.question: Which of the following structures does not form deep relations of the hyoglossus muscle?
questions.explanation: The lingual nerve is a superficial relation of the hyoglossus muscle, not a deep relation.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The lingual nerve is a superficial relation of the hyoglossus muscle, not a deep relation.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Deep fascia and Triangles of the neck
questions.question: You are assessing the post-operative condition of a 65-year-old man who underwent a hemiglossectomy for carcinoma of the tongue. During lymphadenectomy, the posterior triangle lymph nodes were removed. You suspect a nerve injury has occurred. Which of the following movements will you expect to be intact?
questions.explanation: The patient most likely has iatrogenic injury to the spinal accessory nerve in the posterior triangle. Adduction of the arm remains intact because it is produced largely by pectoralis major, supplied by the medial and lateral pectoral nerves.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The patient most likely has iatrogenic injury to the spinal accessory nerve in the posterior triangle. Adduction of the arm remains intact because it is produced largely by pectoralis major, supplied by the medial and lateral pectoral nerves.

questions.question: Which of the following is not the content of the marked triangle?
questions.explanation: The marked region is the subclavian (supraclavicular/omoclavicular) triangle. The dorsal scapular nerve is not a content of this triangle; it is associated with the occipital triangle.

questions.question: While performing a modified radical neck dissection, the surgeon preserves the structure marked below. Which of the following is supplied by this structure?
questions.explanation: The marked structure is the spinal accessory nerve. It enters the posterior triangle by piercing deep to the sternocleidomastoid and crosses the posterior triangle to supply the trapezius. The spinal accessory nerve also supplies sternocleidomastoid.

questions.question: A 1-year-old child diagnosed with roseola infantum has palpable lymph nodes in the region marked in green. Which of the following structures is present here?
questions.explanation: Roseola infantum is a viral fever commonly caused by human herpesvirus 6 and 7. The marked region is the occipital triangle of the posterior triangle. The nerve to rhomboids (dorsal scapular nerve) is among its contents.

questions.question: A patient presents to you with ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis. Which of the following structures marked is most likely to be damaged?
questions.explanation: Ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis suggest Horner syndrome, caused by damage to the cervical sympathetic trunk. In the source cross-sectional image the cervical sympathetic trunk is marked B.
